messages:
alex: Heads-up: prod p99 started stuttering around 11:04 after the mergewave. Seen across redwood-runtime-gpu-1 pool. Noticed spikes in kernel selection latency and batching wait times. Can we triage?

mari: thanks for flagging. saw the alert too. dashboard: https://perf.redwood/inference/streams/mergewave-11-04 -> p99 up ~210ms from baseline.

alex: linking logs: `s3://runtime-logs/prod/2026-03-04/11:04/*` , most tails show `kernel-router` falling back to slow kernel path.

devon: I saw KV cache eviction rates jump around same window. eviction/s = ~3x. Could be interaction: more cache misses > longer seqs > different kernel choice.

sam: is there a minimal repro? can we run `git bisect` between last-known-good and tip of mergewave? I can volunteer to run it if we have a deterministic perf test.

alex: good idea. repro steps I used locally: `./scripts/run_perf_repro.sh --model gpt-large --seq 512 --load-profile prod-traffic.json` . It reproduces p99 locally in ~10 runs.

perf-bot: [alert] CI perf guardrail failed on `main` at 1859340000: p95 latency increased 18%. See job `ci/perf/gate` run 4321.

ci-bot: attached perf artifacts -> `gs://ci-artifacts/4321/flamegraph.svg` and `ci-log.txt` (error: slow-kernel chosen at iteration 120).

mari: devon can you check if any batching heuristic change PR landed in that window? I remember a change to batch floor/ceiling.

devon: scanning PRs between 1859300000..1859340000 -> merged: #4673 `autotune-batcher` and #4678 `kv-cache-lazy-evict` . Both are suspects.

sam: plan: 1) run `git bisect` with the perf repro script (binary search), 2) pin to candidate commits and run a small canary on staging with production traffic. I'll start bisect now.

sam: running: ```
git bisect start
git bisect bad origin/main
git bisect good origin/sha-1859200000
./scripts/run_perf_repro.sh --quick
```

sam: update: bisect narrowed to two commits: 3f2d9a1 (autotune-batcher) and a2b7f4c (kv-cache-lazy-evict). Need manual check.

alex: devon: can you run the perf repro with each patch reverted locally? quick `git revert --no-commit 3f2d9a1` then run perf.

devon: did that. Reverting 3f2d9a1 drops p99 back to baseline. Reverting a2b7f4c has minimal effect.

mari: that points at autotune-batcher change. Any idea what in that PR could switch kernel selection?

devon: autotune now biases towards maximizing batch fullness by increasing wait time ceiling. That increases sequence coalescing, which changes seq-length distribution seen by kernel-selector. The selector then prefers a different kernel variant for medium-length sequences. The new kernel path has regressed perf at higher concurrency.

alex: OK. short-term mitigation: revert 3f2d9a1 on main and ship hotfix. Long-term: tighten selector feature flags and add canary with perf guardrails.

sam: creating revert PR now: #4685 `revert-autotune-batcher-3f2d9a1` -> running CI.

perf-bot: [info] created perf run for revert PR #4685, job ci/perf/gate run 4322.

ci-bot: run 4322 result: perf guardrail passed. p95/p99 restored to baseline.

mari: approved revert after quick codeowner check. scheduling canary deploy to `canary-us-west`.

alex: thanks all. follow-ups: (1) postmortem for autotune PR describing kernel-selection interaction, (2) add small deterministic perf test to catch kernel routing regressions, (3) update rollout checklist to include perf gate for batcher heuristics. I'll own the postmortem.

devon: will open a follow-up PR that splits autotune change into smaller steps with feature flag + perf experiments.

sam: leaving bisect notes in the PR and updating `eng-runtime/triage/wiki` with commands used.

alex: great. closing thread after hotfix completes. :white_check_mark:
